title: Softwood lumber: nominal name to minimum dressed dry size

citation.standard: Voluntary Product Standard PS 20-20, American Softwood Lumber Standard (January 2020)
citation.publisher: U.S. Department of Commerce / National Institute of Standards and Technology, for the American Lumber Standard Committee
citation.where: Table 3, "Nominal and minimum-dressed sizes of boards, dimension, and timbers", page 16 — the Dry columns (thicknesses and widths), which are the sizes of lumber at 19 percent or less moisture content (§2.7, §6.2.3). The Green columns of the same table are deliberately not carried; see the note below.

entries.name: 1x2
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 19 mm (3/4 in) dry. Widths: nominal 2 in -> 38 mm (1-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 1x3
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 3/4 in dry. Widths: nominal 3 in -> 64 mm (2-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 1x4
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 3/4 in dry. Widths: nominal 4 in -> 89 mm (3-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 1x6
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 3/4 in dry. Widths: nominal 6 in -> 140 mm (5-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 1x8
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 3/4 in dry. Widths: nominal 8 in -> 184 mm (7-1/4 in) dry — the step where the standard stops taking 1/2 in off and starts taking 3/4 in.

entries.name: 1x10
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 3/4 in dry. Widths: nominal 10 in -> 235 mm (9-1/4 in) dry.

entries.name: 1x12
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 3/4 in dry. Widths: nominal 12 in -> 286 mm (11-1/4 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x2
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 38 mm (1-1/2 in) dry. Widths: nominal 2 in -> 38 mm (1-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x3
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 1-1/2 in dry. Widths: nominal 3 in -> 64 mm (2-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x4
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 38 mm (1-1/2 in) dry. Widths: nominal 4 in -> 89 mm (3-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x6
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 1-1/2 in dry. Widths: nominal 6 in -> 140 mm (5-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x8
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 1-1/2 in dry. Widths: nominal 8 in -> 184 mm (7-1/4 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x10
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 1-1/2 in dry. Widths: nominal 10 in -> 235 mm (9-1/4 in) dry.

entries.name: 2x12
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 2 in -> 1-1/2 in dry. Widths: nominal 12 in -> 286 mm (11-1/4 in) dry.

entries.name: 3x3
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 3 in -> 64 mm (2-1/2 in) dry. Widths: nominal 3 in -> 64 mm (2-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 4x4
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension — a 4x4 is dimension lumber and not a timber, because PS 20-20 §3.4.2 puts everything from nominal 2 in up to but not including nominal 5 in thick in that class. Thicknesses: nominal 4 in -> 89 mm (3-1/2 in) dry. Widths: nominal 4 in -> 89 mm (3-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 4x6
entries.derivation: Table 3, Dimension. Thicknesses: nominal 4 in -> 3-1/2 in dry. Widths: nominal 6 in -> 140 mm (5-1/2 in) dry.

entries.name: 6x6
entries.derivation: Table 3, Timbers, which states an amount taken off the nominal size rather than a finished cell. Thicknesses, 5 & 6 thick: 13 mm (1/2 in) off dry, so 6 - 1/2 = 5-1/2 in. Widths, 5 & 6 wide: 1/2 in off, so 6 - 1/2 = 5-1/2 in.

entries.name: 6x8
entries.derivation: Table 3, Timbers. Thicknesses, 5 & 6 thick: 1/2 in off dry, so 6 - 1/2 = 5-1/2 in. Widths, 7-15 wide: 19 mm (3/4 in) off dry, so 8 - 3/4 = 7-1/4 in.

entries.name: 8x8
entries.derivation: Table 3, Timbers. Thicknesses, 7-15 thick: 19 mm (3/4 in) off dry, so 8 - 3/4 = 7-1/4 in. Widths, 7-15 wide: 3/4 in off dry, so 8 - 3/4 = 7-1/4 in.
